solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Receives information about Turkey's earliest football club

indicators.note: the word for receiving information goes around the letter taken from Turkey

parts.note: to receive information is to hear (of) it, giving hears

indicators.note: earliest asks for the first letter of the word Turkey's

explanation.surface: A reporter learns about the oldest football club in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey's' looks like the country; only its first letter is used. HEARTS (Heart of Midlothian) is an Edinburgh football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is the familiar name of a Scottish professional football club based in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Servant reportedly assigned by agency

indicators.note: by places the word for agency alongside, before the spoken word

parts.note: having a hand in something means acting through agency, as in 'by the hand of'

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for assigned is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: made in the sense of appointed or assigned to a role

explanation.surface: A domestic is supposedly placed with a household through an employment agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agency' means acting through someone, as in 'by the hand of'. Taking made to mean assigned is a stretch, as the blogger notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaid is a female personal servant or attendant, an old-fashioned word for a maid.

clue.text: Treatise on muscles is hard to understand

indicators.note: in a down clue the treatise sits on top of, i.e. after, the muscles

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
a tract is a short treatise or pamphlet

explanation.surface: A scholarly paper on anatomy is impenetrable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treatise' wants to be the definition, since an abstract is a summary of a paper; it is TRACT, and the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract ideas are theoretical rather than concrete, and so difficult to grasp.

clue.text: Evident in umpteenth oracle from God

indicators.note: evident in says the letters can be seen within the words umpteenth oracle

explanation.surface: A god speaks through the countless oracles consulted.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder, wielder of the hammer Mjolnir.

clue.text: Supports accepting old fellow's plan

indicators.note: accepting means the word for supports takes the abbreviation for old inside it

parts.note: props are supports holding something up
Al is a stock crossword man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: An elderly man's scheme rests on backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a scheme or suggestion put forward for consideration.

clue.text: Blues singer with good range initially all at sea

indicators.note: all at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into a new order
initially takes the first letters of good and range

explanation.surface: A blues vocalist with a fine range has lost their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' mixes SINGER, WITH and the initials G and R. 'Blues' looks musical; in Britain Blues are Conservatives, whose party colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservatives are the political right, so British Tories, known by their blue colours, are right-wingers.

clue.text: Very noticeable when once proud knight breaks down

indicators.note: something that breaks down falls apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A once-proud knight's collapse is plain for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' rearranges ONCE PROUD with N.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronounced feature is strongly marked or distinct, easy to see.

clue.text: Soviet leader's son to finish off story at home

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: finishing off the word means removing its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A dictator's boy completes his tale while staying in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to finish off' removes the final E of TALE. The 's of 'leader's' is the link 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin led the Soviet Union from the 1920s until his death in 1953.

clue.text: Longing to hug withdrawn Italian musician

indicators.note: to hug means the word for longing wraps around the other piece

parts.note: lust is strong longing or desire

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: It is a short form of Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A shy Italian performer is embraced by desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' is the reversal signal, not shyness; 'to hug' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutist is a player of the lute, a stringed instrument, so a kind of musician.

clue.text: Someone not turning up with food immediately lacks a bit of neighbourliness

indicators.note: with joins the word for food to what follows

parts.note: nosh is informal British slang for food

indicators.note: lacks means the word for immediately goes without the given letter

parts.note: now means immediately

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the first letter of neighbourliness

explanation.surface: A guest who never arrives for dinner shows poor neighbourly spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' drops N, the first letter of 'neighbourliness', from NOW to leave OW.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is a person who books or is expected but fails to appear.

clue.text: Unaware of refusal to stand by soldier over angry tirade

indicators.note: to stand by places the refusal right beside the soldier
over means turned over, so the soldier's letters are read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
no is a refusal
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A soldier, ignorant of the order, refuses to stand by during an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is an American soldier; 'over' turns it round before the refusal and the tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant of something means lacking knowledge of it, oblivious to it.

clue.text: Bishop to sense trouble over truth about female patron

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: over means the jumbled letters sit across the top of, enclosing, the next pieces
trouble means to disturb, so the letters of sense are stirred up

parts.note: a fact is a truth
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A bishop senses unease over the truth about a female sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' makes ENESS from the letters of sense; in a down clue 'over' lets those letters wrap the pieces below.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactress is a woman who gives money or help, a female backer or sponsor.

clue.text: Earth wiped from Scottish weapon again

indicators.note: wiped from means the earth is removed from the weapon's name

parts.note: a claymore is a large Scottish broadsword
clay is earth or soil

explanation.surface: Someone cleans the soil off a Scottish sword for another go.
explanation.definitionFit: In phrases like 'once more' the word means additionally, one further time.

clue.text: Set limit of difficult words often repeated in literary works

definitions.text: words often repeated in literary works

indicators.note: difficult letters are troublesome ones, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to fix a ceiling on hard vocabulary in books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges SET LIMIT OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurring theme or phrase, used in music and by extension in novels and poems.

clue.text: Single aunt hated Dicky without a hint of contrition

indicators.note: without means outside, so the jumbled letters surround the hint
dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters are rearranged
a hint of takes just the first letter of contrition

explanation.surface: An unmarried aunt loathed a man called Dicky and felt no remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but means unsound, rearranging AUNT HATED around C; 'without' here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unattached describes someone not married or in a relationship, i.e. single.

clue.text: Girl almost entering where nuns may be found causing trouble

indicators.note: entering means the shortened name goes inside the phrase for where nuns live

parts.note: nuns live in a convent, so they are found in convent

indicators.note: almost means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl nearly joining a nunnery is making a nuisance of herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ENID to ENI, which goes into IN CONVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconvenient creates difficulty or awkwardness for those affected.

clue.text: Silent about foreboding at the launch of this political movement

indicators.note: about means the word for silent goes around the other pieces

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
an omen is a foreboding sign

indicators.note: at the launch of takes the first letter of this

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about misgivings when a new political group is founded.
explanation.walkthrough: Momentum is a left-wing grassroots group in the British Labour Party, founded in 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the name of a UK campaigning organisation backing the Labour left.

clue.text: Extreme admiration for an artificial language experiment involving the French

indicators.note: involving means the two pieces take the French article inside

parts.note: Ido is a constructed language derived from Esperanto
a try is an attempt or experiment
la is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone is besotted with an invented-language project that includes French.
explanation.walkthrough: Ido is a real constructed language, a reformed Esperanto; 'involving' sets the French article inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry literally means worship of idols, and figuratively excessive devotion to someone.

clue.text: Unusually long halters on donkeys at the front giving complete control

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after
unusually signals the letters appear in an unusual order
at the front takes the first letter of donkeys

explanation.surface: Extra-long halters on the leading donkeys keep them fully in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges LONG HALTERS, and D from 'donkeys' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranglehold is literally a choking grip and figuratively a total, restrictive domination.

clue.text: Soldiers having excellent parking in front of living accommodation

indicators.note: in front of places the parking letter before the soldiers

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
fab is slang for fabulous, excellent

explanation.surface: Troops enjoy great parking outside their quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: A prefab is a prefabricated house, common in postwar Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a factory-built house assembled on site, so a place to live.

clue.text: In charge after France occupies areas of the second largest continent

indicators.note: occupies means the letters move inside the two areas

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for area, doubled for areas

indicators.note: after places the charge letters following the ones for France

explanation.surface: France, now in charge, takes over territories on a vast continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'areas' gives two A's, one for each area, which 'occupies' fills from within.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is second only to Asia in both area and population among continents.

clue.text: Stubborn resistance seen in workplace on the outskirts of Rochdale

indicators.note: on means the workplace is placed after the outskirts in an across clue
the outskirts are the outer letters of Rochdale
seen in means the resistance letter appears inside the workplace

parts.note: a factory is a workplace
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Dogged opposition at a mill on the edge of a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Rochdale is a former mill town near Manchester; only its first and last letters RE are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory describes a person or thing that resists control, obstinate and unmanageable.

clue.text: Advisable for a supplier of water

definitions.meaning: advisable in the sense of wise
a shaft sunk to draw water from underground

explanation.definitionFit: The word means wise or sensible in 'as well', and a bore drawing water from the ground.

clue.text: Ceremony's just on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: just means fair or right

explanation.surface: A fair ceremony is being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a religious or solemn ritual, a formal observance.

clue.text: Restore to a normal position following earlier alarm

indicators.note: earlier means the following letter comes first

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to righten something is to set it upright again

explanation.surface: Setting something straight after an earlier scare.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to scare or startle them.

clue.text: Tease about finding tasteless articles in some kind of order

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for tease is read backwards

parts.note: to kid is to tease
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: Mocking someone for finding tacky goods in their order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the word for tease, giving DIK.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh decree imposed without consultation, a kind of command.

clue.text: Island hit at the outset by a particular kind of wave

indicators.note: by means the brand stands next to, before, the island pieces

parts.note: a brand is a particular kind or variety

indicators.note: at the outset takes the first letter of hit

explanation.surface: An island is struck first by a certain type of sea wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wave' at the end looks part of the seascape, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a weapon is to wave or flourish it about.

clue.text: Suitable space found in Spain's capital city

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of Spain's
found in means the space sits inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Room found in Spain's capital city that is fit for purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital city' suggests Madrid, but 'capital' takes S and the city is ELY, a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly behaviour is proper and fitting by accepted standards.
